_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); orders, revenue and margin signals; the listing and short-history bounds rules

pit_profile.why: Baker Hughes: 'an energy technology company with a diversified portfolio of technologies and services that span the energy and industrial value chain'; 'Our revenue is predominately generated from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'may shift demand from oil and natural gas towards an investment in relatively lower carbon emitting energy sources and alternative energy solutions' (its own FY2024 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' spending on exploration, development and production through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which an oilfield services and equipment company does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: Baker Hughes: 'an energy technology company with a diversified portfolio of technologies and services that span the energy and industrial value chain'; 'Our revenue is predominately generated from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'may shift demand from oil and natural gas towards an investment in relatively lower carbon emitting energy sources and alternative energy solutions' (its own FY2024 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' spending on exploration, development and production through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which an oilfield services and equipment company does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.11x; +24% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.65; conservative 2yr +10%.

BEAR.desc: EPS +0.0%/yr (worst year FY18-FY24 ex-FY19 ex-FY20 ex-FY21, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -1.3%/yr (Q2 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 7.7-yr ex-FY17 ex-FY19 ex-FY20 ex-FY21 median

BULL.desc: EPS +31.7%/yr (FY18-FY24 ex-FY19 ex-FY20 ex-FY21 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +60.7%/yr (best 2-yr run FY18-FY24 ex-FY19 ex-FY20 ex-FY21, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: BKR (retrospective, 2025-09-12) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.11x (26.9% downside to Bear $34 / +235.6% upside to Bull $156) | Adj composite 2.20 vs market 1.55: gap +0.65 [UNDERVALUED] | +24% above the EPP floor $38 (16x FY25E $2.35) | Conservative 2-yr case: +10.2% total (+5.1%/yr) | At 19.8x FY25E the 15% hurdle price $61 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; orders -6.6% and revenue -3.2% in Q2 2025, forward revenues -3.2% (no Q3 2025 revenue guide, Q2 2025 revenue as reported); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; no theme in scope has dated evidence.
